blocks.title: Disproportionation reaction
blocks.text: A disproportionation reaction is a chemical reaction in which a single substance acts as both the oxidising and the reducing agent, giving two different products with different oxidation states: the same element is simultaneously oxidised and reduced.

The decomposition of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen, 2H2O2 giving 2H2O + O2, is a disproportionation: oxygen is -1 in H2O2, -2 in H2O (reduced from -1 to -2) and 0 in O2 (oxidised from -1 to 0). Similarly chlorine with sodium hydroxide, 3Cl2 + 6NaOH giving 5NaCl + NaClO3 + 3H2O: chlorine is 0 in Cl2, -1 in NaCl (reduced from 0 to -1) and +5 in NaClO3 (oxidised from 0 to +5). Disproportionation can occur where ions or molecules can exist in several oxidation states.
Identify the species that undergoes both oxidation and reduction in 3HNO2 giving HNO3 + 2NO + H2O.
